title: Calabria's Pumps Keep Climbing: Diesel Nears €2.20 as the Region Outpaces Italy
dek: Four straight days of increases have pushed Calabria's self-service Benzina and Gasolio prices above the national average.
body: Drivers filling up in Calabria are paying €1.9933 per litre for self-service Benzina and €2.2044 for self-service Gasolio as of July 24, 2026 — both running above Italy's national self-service averages of €1.9807 and €2.1856 respectively. That works out to roughly a 1.3-cent premium on petrol and a nearly 1.9-cent premium on diesel compared with the rest of the country.

The trend line only points one way: over the last four tracked days, Calabria's self-service Benzina rose from €1.9683 to €1.9933 (+2.5 cents), while Gasolio climbed even faster, from €2.1468 to €2.2044 (+5.76 cents), rising every single day without a pause. The region's station network tells a quieter story: 711 of Calabria's 793 registered stations reported prices today, down slightly from 715 of 794 a day earlier — a small dip in daily reporting activity worth watching.

Tracking four fuels across twenty regions, every day, without a single manual spreadsheet update, is only realistic because Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself automatically each morning. The entire pipeline — pulling the raw MIMIT feed, crunching the numbers, picking today's regional spotlight, and republishing the site — runs unattended, built with Claude Code.
pull_quote: Calabria's diesel price has climbed for four consecutive days, now running nearly 2 cents above Italy's national self-service average.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Calabria, where diesel is closing in on €2.20 a litre.

Self-service Gasolio in Calabria hit €2.2044 per litre on July 24 — up nearly 6 cents in just four days and now running above Italy's €2.1856 national average. Benzina told the same story, climbing to €1.9933 against a €1.9807 national average.

Fuel Dashboard tracks self-service and served prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL, and Metano across all 20 Italian regions, refreshed daily straight from the MIMIT open-data feed. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

What I find most interesting isn't the price move itself — it's how it was built. This entire dashboard, including today's regional writeup, is generated automatically every morning by Claude Code: no manual Excel file, no copy-pasting yesterday's numbers, no human recalculating averages. A few years ago this would have been a part-time analyst's job. Now it's a script that runs before breakfast. That's the real story of what AI coding tools change — not replacing analysis, but making daily, granular, per-region reporting cheap enough to actually do.
